Neurodevelopmental impairment and distal skeletal abnormalities define syndrome; ptosis reported in 3/3. Other structural organ abnormalities have only isolated reports.
Mature B-cell leukemia/lymphoma involving blood, marrow or lymphoid tissue; lymphoma warrants the immune mechanism axis.
Oral and digital malformations with Joubert-type brain abnormalities define syndrome; hydronephrosis in the single reported patient (1/1).
Calcifications of the reproductive testis; no demonstrated gonadal endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ disease.
Tumor originates in the fallopian tube, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Recurrent infantile liver failure; vertebral and femoral epiphyseal abnormalities in 3/3 establish common skeletal involvement. Prolonged PT reflects hepatic synthetic failure.
Defined by skeletal dysplasia, camptodactyly and multiple limb/joint malformations; microcephaly without demonstrated neurologic dysfunction does not add an axis.
Umbrella for diseases of the liver; endocrine and extrahepatic involvement are not shared defining features.
Developmental disability and sinus-node dysfunction define syndrome; retinal functional abnormality on ERG occurs in 30-79%. Reflux is a separately diagnosed disease.
Congenital nystagmus with impaired binocular vision and ocular alignment; no additional neurologic disease established.
Peripheral nerve hyperexcitability syndrome causing cramps and fasciculations; muscle symptoms do not establish myocyte damage. Autoimmunity is not universal.
Classic forms predominate: lens dislocation and skeletal disease often >50%, neurodevelopmental injury ~50%. Vascular disease omitted by cap; remethylation forms differ.
Severe congenital brain malformations; contractures in 4/6 and talipes in 3/3 establish skeletal involvement. Isolated eye/heart reports do not establish ≥30% across the cohort.
Intellectual and language impairment in 18/18 with frequent macrocephaly; hypotonia and motor delay do not establish separate muscle disease.
Beckwith-Wiedemann features include defining macroglossia/abdominal-wall defects and hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia. Organ enlargement and tumor predisposition alone add no axes.
Defined skeletal-muscle disease caused by an inborn defect of the malate-aspartate metabolic shuttle; no supported additional organ involvement.
Treatment-resistant hematopoietic or lymphoid malignancy; lymphoma and specific extra-marrow organ involvement are not shared across this umbrella.
Skin blistering/aplasia and pyloric atresia define disease; urinary tract abnormalities collectively 30-79%. Muscular dystrophy is occasional (5-29%), excluded.
Syndactyly and intellectual disability define syndrome. Hirsutism, thick hair and dermatoglyphic differences do not establish damaging skin disease.
Congenital abnormal, nonfunctioning lung tissue within a pulmonary lobe; its systemic arterial supply does not establish separate cardiovascular damage.
Progressive degeneration of frontal and temporal brain regions causes dementia, behavioral change and language impairment.
Adenocarcinoma originates in the urethra, which belongs to the renal/urinary axis.
Benign neoplasm of the parathyroid endocrine gland; no additional organ damage is established for this histologic subtype.
Benign vascular lesion arising in and occupying the rectal wall; both rectal location and blood-vessel origin define it.
